scope: Broadened research across independent DWG/DXF/ACIS projects, downstream CAD consumers, and the ODA DataStorage record-boundary rule

method.kind: static review of current primary project source/docs, live issue reports, and local ODA v5.4.1 text
method.sourcePinning: Mutable GitHub main/master and docs.rs latest pages were read on 2026-10-15; pin exact revisions/builds before any external execution.
method.evidenceRule: Project README claims and issue-reported measurements are leads only. Distinguish parser, geometry kernel, display, and target-consumer evidence; no single category promotes support.

findings.evidence: OpenCADStudio advertises native DWG/DXF R14-R2018 workflows and desktop releases for Windows, Linux, and Apple Silicon macOS. Its documented ACIS display route parses SAT/SAB, attempts to lift bodies into opencadkernel B-rep and triangulate faces, and has a per-surface fallback which marks incomplete meshes. opencadkernel describes itself as early, with most operations not yet implemented. The codec repository is a fork in the ACadRust lineage, not an independent parser family from ACadRust.
findings.confidence: Project source/docs and code-family relationship; no binary execution or independent file inspection in this review.
findings.planUse: Add as a candidate cross-platform non-OCCT consumer and distinct custom-kernel lineage. It may support target-display/mesh completeness checks after pinning; it is not yet a stand-alone exact B-rep oracle. Require exact version, supported SAT/SAB profile, file hash, body/handle inventory, no incomplete fallback, and a source-authored expected manifest.

findings.evidence: A maintainer reports that a same-version DWG writer correction retained non-entity DataStorage links with the unchanged AcDs section and produced a byte-identical 613-segment AcDs section for the supplied source pair. The same report documents earlier layout/MLeader corruption and says the fix was validated against its supplied case.
findings.confidence: Issue maintainer report, not independently rerun here and not normative format evidence.
findings.planUse: Prioritize a conservative unchanged-section passthrough path before general AcDs/SAB writer synthesis. Bind reuse to the exact source section/version, linked body handles, source payload hashes, and unchanged geometry/reference graph. Any solid edit, erase, owner change, or handle remap must invalidate passthrough or use a qualified regeneration route; a no-op byte copy cannot establish editable geometry support.

findings.evidence: Open issue #1411 reports that an AC1032 REGION's 5,489-byte SAB body is lost through LibreDWG DXF-to-DWG-to-DXF conversion while its entity remains; a separate confidential AutoCAD 2018 case reportedly loses 88 bodies. Current source contains an AcDs section reader, which is compatible with the distinction between section recognition and complete DataStorage/body association.
findings.confidence: Issue reproductions and confidential sample were not executed or independently inspected; repository source is a mutable snapshot.
findings.planUse: Keep per-leg source-handle, has-data/empty-state, AcDs record, body payload hash and target disposition checks. Entity-count equality or successful conversion is not a 3D pass.

sources: local reference: Open Design Specification v5.4.1, section 24.2.2.3, printed pages 254-256
findings.evidence: ODA defines each data record's maximum readable span from the next consecutive data-stream offset, or the data-segment end for the last record. An inline record is valid only when the 4-byte size field plus dataSize fits that span. The direct-byte-array limit is 0x40000; larger values use the explicit blob-reference marker. At baseline 5eaa61a the local reader bounded direct payloads by the segment end but did not apply the next-record span or 0x40000 limit. The follow-on in-memory reproducer demonstrated both violations, and the working-tree change now enforces the bounds.
findings.confidence: Normative ODA statement cross-checked against local source; the baseline gap was reproduced and the focused local fix passed its targeted test. Producer-profile coverage remains open.
findings.planUse: Keep the checked per-segment ordered offset map and adjacent-record bounds for inline payloads and complete blob descriptors. Retain exact 0x40000 acceptance, direct 0x40001 rejection, overlap rejection, and following-record survival as regression controls. Keep inputs generated in memory; continue with multi-page aggregate-size and page-reference hardening.

findings.evidence: FreeCAD's current format guide describes stock DXF/DWG conversion/import as 2D-only because 3D ACIS payloads are proprietary; issue #18454 says the ordinary DXF importer cannot read those blobs. This confirms that the standard FreeCAD Linux/Windows qualification is a 2D and truthful-loss gate, not an ACIS semantic oracle.
findings.confidence: Current project documentation and maintainer issue response; exact native FreeCAD builds/importer modes still require runtime qualification.
findings.planUse: Keep native Linux and Windows FreeCAD acceptance scoped to the configured stock importer/converter and represented 2D/explicit entities. Keep ACIS shape semantics on a separately named kernel/plugin route.

findings.evidence: InventorLoader advertises SAT/SAB and DXF-solid import and its source contains ACIS/SAB parsing through FreeCAD Part/OCCT. The GitHub repository LICENSE page contains GPL-2.0 text while the FreeCAD Addon Report labels the add-on LGPL-3.0-or-later, a metadata/source-license discrepancy. The project documents unsupported ACIS constructs and is not a DWG AcDs parser.
findings.confidence: Public repo/docs metadata; license conflict must be resolved against exact file notices/maintainer terms before reuse.
findings.planUse: Keep it optional as an external parser/OCCT comparison only. Do not copy, link, or redistribute its code until license provenance is reconciled; do not count it as a distinct geometry kernel from FreeCAD.

findings.evidence: ACadRust documents a pure-Rust SAT/SAB/DWG/DXF implementation; acis-core explicitly says model reference closure is not B-rep validity and does not itself construct OCCT solids. cq-acis converts only supported profiles/shapes to CadQuery/OCCT and calls the project experimental.
findings.confidence: Current project documentation; exact release and profile must be pinned before execution.
findings.planUse: Use Rust-owned parser/reference-closure output as a structural differential only; use cq-acis/FreeCAD as one shared OCCT geometry lineage; never count the parser and geometry adapter as two independent kernels.

readinessChanges: Implement ODA adjacent-record bounds and direct/blob threshold vectors before continuing higher-level AcDs writer work.
After local bounded extraction is stable, separate same-version unchanged AcDs raw passthrough from edited/new-body synthesis; stale handle or payload fingerprints must refuse reuse.
Add pinned OpenCADStudio as a possible Linux/Windows/macOS consumer checkpoint for complete visible 3D tessellation, not as a current exact-shape oracle.
Keep native FreeCAD standard import qualification focused on 2D/explicit-entity and no-silent-loss behavior; do not wait for its expected ACIS importer limitation to implement local parsing.

validation.projectBuild: Targeted libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests and lc3_compat_check build PASS after the follow-on local parser change
validation.tests: libdxfrw_graph_preservation CTest PASS 1/1; full suite not run
